An active recovery record refuses only when -not $DryRun; a dry run just records the refusal text.
Enter-TaskLock runs only in real runs, so foreground validation never probes lock availability.

findings.verification: With CODEX_CONSULT_EXE unset and codex off PATH, run the proposed foreground validation; if it exits 0, the gap is real.

findings.claim: The design gives no mechanism that writes a terminal status on every background exit path: Stop-WithError and the direct exit 0/1 sites bypass any maintain-the-status-file duty, so a background refused after start (lock, active record, launcher, store parse) leaves the file at starting/running forever and -Status then reports it died with a recovery message that is false (nothing was started, nothing to recover).
findings.trigger: Any Stop-WithError reached by the background process after the foreground has handed over, e.g. lock refusal at codex-consult.ps1:1984 or panel refusal at 1242.

evidence.observation: Stop-WithError prints and calls exit 1 directly; no status hook exists.
Multiple direct exit sites inside try blocks; only task-lock/store cleanup runs in finally, no detached-status write is plumbed.
The brief says the background ALSO maintains the file at start/per-member/end but names no interception of refusal exits.

findings.verification: Kill-test variant: hold the task lock, then -Detach; after the background exits 1, run -Status and check whether the file reached state done with exit 1 or stuck at starting.
findings.remedy: Wrap the entire background main in a script-scope finally (or extend Stop-WithError to honor -DetachId) that idempotently writes {state done, exit <code>, summary: the last error/success line} on every exit, and add the refused-after-start test.

findings.claim: -Wait's proposed default timeout (timeout + retries + 120 s) is one member's kill guard, not the run's budget: panels serialize same-endpoint members, so a legitimate panel outlives the default and -Wait exits 3 still running; moreover the proposed status schema has no field -Wait could read a default from.
findings.trigger: A detached panel whose largest endpoint group has more members than its limit (the default limit is 1 per endpoint).

evidence.observation: The guard is TimeoutSec + 60 + 120 (+ repair/denial budgets) per member.
Get-PanelPlan builds endpoint groups whose members run one after another unless the roster raises the limit; -PanelConcurrency can serialize everything.

evidence.reference: Design item 2 status schema {id, started, state, exit, task, kind, members, summary, log}
evidence.observation: No timeout/budget/plan field exists.

findings.verification: Detach a fakes panel with two members of one endpoint and -WaitTimeoutSec default; observe exit 3 while members still run.
findings.remedy: Compute the critical-path bound (ceil(max group size / limit) x guard + slack, capped by -PanelConcurrency) at detach time, store budget_sec in the status file, and default -WaitTimeoutSec to it plus margin.

findings.claim: The status file's first-write ownership is unspecified and racy: the foreground writes state starting (it cannot know the background pid yet), and if the background's own first write lands first, a foreground write after Start-Process overwrites running with stale starting; a single run has no intermediate member updates, so the file can read starting until the terminal write, and a background that dies before its first write leaves a pid-less file whose liveness cannot be judged at all.
findings.trigger: Slow foreground bookkeeping after Start-Process, or a background that fails before parsing -DetachId (bad host, script moved, parameter refusal).

evidence.observation: The existing child-launch pattern (Start-Process then slot bookkeeping) shows the write-after-start ordering the design would copy.

evidence.reference: Design items 1-2 (foreground writes the first version; the file records the background pid + start time)
evidence.observation: Two writers with no ordering rule; neither is designated to own the pid.

findings.verification: Instrument fakes so the background writes running within 50 ms while the foreground sleeps 500 ms before its write; then read the file: state starting.
findings.remedy: The foreground writes starting (no pid) only BEFORE launching and never after; the background's first action after parsing -DetachId is an atomic self-report write {state running, pid, start_time, host}; -Status treats starting+no-pid as just started, retry.

findings.remedy: Define the aggregate as the worst state (running > failed > ok), print every match, and refuse with a distinct exit code when an id8 prefix matches more than one file.

findings.claim: The design contradicts itself on writing (-Status -Wait take no lock and write nothing, yet -Status -Prune deletes files), does not say the background must be started with the foreground's working directory, and does not refuse -Detach together with the internal -PanelSpec: relative -Brief/-Artifact/-CollabDir resolve against callerCwd, so a background with a different cwd validates against the wrong files.
findings.trigger: -Detach with relative paths where the launched background inherits a different working directory, or a user passing -Detach -PanelSpec.

evidence.observation: Brief and artifact resolution walks @($callerCwd, $repoRoot); the panel brief probe does the same at 1192-1196.
Item 3 forbids writes, item 6 adds deletion; neither the working directory nor -PanelSpec refusal is mentioned.

findings.verification: -Detach with -Brief given as a relative path that only exists under the coordinator's cwd, launched without -WorkingDirectory: the background refuses brief not found.
findings.remedy: Say -Prune is the one writing form of -Status, refuse -Detach with -PanelSpec (and -DryRun/-Status/-Wait as planned), and always Start-Process the background with -WorkingDirectory set to the foreground's cwd.

findings.claim: An unreadable status file (present but empty, unparseable, no id, bad state) is never pruned - -Status -Prune skips the `unreadable` judgement - and the SessionStart hook counts it in the died phrase indefinitely, so one corrupted file permanently degrades -Status (exit 1), -List and the hook with no cleanup path.
findings.trigger: A .consult.detached-<id8>.status.json corrupted or truncated by an external writer, then more than 7 days later -Status -Prune.

evidence.observation: The prune loop continues past every run whose judgement is not done/died/never-started; `unreadable` is not in the list, and its Record is null so no age is even computed.
Get-DetachedPhrase maps died, never-started AND unreadable into the permanent `died` category.

findings.verification: Fabricate an unparseable .consult.detached-deadbeef.status.json with an old file time, run -Status -Prune, and observe the file still present and still counted by the hook phrase.
findings.remedy: Treat `unreadable` as prunable after the same 7-day window (using the file's last-write time, as Read-DetachedRuns already records), or add -Prune -Force for unreadable files.

findings.claim: After the 60-second grace a `starting` record without a pid is reported as never started with the categorical wording `nothing was run`, but a slow background (cold start, antivirus, >60 s host spin-up) may still self-report afterwards and turn the record into running - the transient judgement can state a falsehood and, in -Prune's view, mark the run prunable as never-started 7 days later even though it ran.
findings.trigger: A machine where spawning the hidden host plus parsing the 4,600-line script takes more than the fixed 60 s grace between the foreground's write and the background's self-report.

evidence.observation: The grace is a fixed $script:DetachedStartGraceSec = 60; past it the text asserts nothing was run.
The self-report happens only after the host started, resolved the repo/collab roots and read the status file - measurable delay on a cold machine.

evidence.reference: Windows process start under AV scan
evidence.observation: Spin-up beyond 60 s is plausible; not measured here.

findings.verification: Suspend the background process at start (or add a test hook delaying the self-report), run -Status after 61 s, then resume: observe never-started wording followed by a record that becomes running.
findings.remedy: Word the never-started text conditionally (`no background process reported within 60 s ... its log may say why` already helps; drop `nothing was run` or add `if it started at all`), and let -Prune also require the log to be absent or empty before treating never-started as never having run.

findings.claim: The SessionStart hook now dot-sources the entire codex-consult-common.ps1 (~7,100 lines) in its own process on every session start, in addition to spawning codex-providers.ps1 - a small but permanent latency addition to every session for one phrase.
findings.trigger: Every Claude Code session start in a repository with the plugin enabled.

evidence.observation: The new try block dot-sources common and calls Get-DetachedPhrase; before wave 25 the hook started no other PowerShell parsing beyond its child process.
Parsing 7,100 lines typically costs a few hundred ms; not measured here.

findings.verification: Time the hook (`Measure-Command` around its invocation) at HEAD and at c4cb428 in the same repo; compare.
findings.remedy: Accept the cost, or split the detached-run readers (Read-DetachedRuns, Get-DetachedJudgement, Get-DetachedPhrase) into a small file the hook can dot-source alone.

findings.claim: Unreadable detached status files are reported as failures but are excluded from every pruneable state, so corrupt or truncated status and log files accumulate forever even though the declared deviation groups unreadable files under the died/never-started family.
findings.trigger: A detached status file becomes empty, truncated or invalid JSON, then ages past seven days and -Status -Prune runs.

evidence.observation: Problems produce judgement state unreadable with exit 1.
Prune deletes only done, died and never-started; unreadable is skipped and cannot supply timestamps anyway.

findings.verification: Create a `.consult.detached-aaaaaaaa.status.json` containing invalid JSON, backdate both files by eight days, then run `-Status -Prune` and observe that neither file is removed.
findings.remedy: Let prune handle unreadable files by file timestamps after seven days, or add an explicit corrupt-state policy and document its retention rule.

findings.claim: Status persistence is deliberately best-effort and both intermediate and final write errors are swallowed, so a successful detached run can exit 0 while its status remains running or starting and later appears died.
findings.trigger: The status path becomes read-only, locked, full or otherwise unwritable after the background self-report but before a member or terminal update.

evidence.observation: Save-DetachedRun catches every update failure and continues.
Complete-DetachedRun catches the terminal write failure and does not change the process exit code.

findings.verification: Run a faked detached consultation to completion while denying writes to its status file after self-report; compare the background exit 0 and complete log summary against a non-done status record.
findings.remedy: Retry terminal writes with bounded backoff and, if persistence still fails, return a distinct non-zero exit while printing that the completed result exists only in the log.

findings.claim: Killing only the detached background panel parent process leaves its child member processes running, as documented.
findings.trigger: User kills the detached background process of a panel run.

evidence.observation: Panel parent has no finally block that kills members; members are independent processes with their own recovery records.
Brief explicitly lists this as a known, accepted deviation.

findings.verification: Start a detached panel, kill the background pid, run -Status and observe it reports died while members still run.
findings.remedy: No fix required; this is an accepted tradeoff for the no-daemon design. Member recovery records will be handled correctly by the next run.

findings.claim: A status file that matches the detached glob but cannot be parsed (or names no id / bad state) is judged 'unreadable' (exit 1), poisons every aggregate -Status/-Wait of the task, and can never be removed by -Status -Prune: the prune loop only deletes done/died/never-started, so the only recourse is deleting the file by hand.
findings.trigger: Any file matching .consult.detached-*.status.json that is empty, truncated (crash mid-write is unlikely given atomic replace, but hand edits / disk-full partials happen), or hand-fabricated without an id; then -Task <t> -Status with no -Id.

evidence.observation: Get-DetachedJudgement returns State 'unreadable', Exit 1 when $Problem is set (empty/unparseable/non-object/no-id/bad-state file).
Prune loop continues unless judgement state is done/died/never-started, so unreadable files are always skipped; the worst-state exit loop then still counts their exit 1.
Read-DetachedRuns accepts any name matching .consult.detached-<alnum>.status.json, so a stray non-hex file becomes an 'unreadable' run.

findings.verification: Write garbage into a .consult.detached-zz99.status.json, run -Status (expect exit 1) then -Status -Prune, re-run -Status and confirm the file is still there and exit is still 1.
findings.remedy: Let -Status -Prune delete unreadable files older than 7 days too (or refuse them explicitly with the manual-delete command), and cover it in harness-detach FABRIC/prune cases.

findings.claim: The foreground's `starting` record embeds the background's full arguments (base64 CLIXML), including an inline -Prompt text, in a repo file; the background drops `args` at self-report, but if it never starts the arguments linger in the status file indefinitely (until manual deletion).
findings.trigger: -Detach with -Prompt '<text>' (rather than -Brief file) where the background never reports (bad host, deleted script).

evidence.observation: Starting record built with args = ConvertTo-DetachArgs(bgArgs) where bgArgs is every bound parameter incl. Prompt; written before launch.
Background clears args ($dRec.args = $null) only when it reaches self-report; a background that never starts leaves the foreground file untouched.
Record comment confirms args live only in the foreground's starting record.

findings.verification: Detach with inline -Prompt and a poisoned script path, then decode the .status.json args field and confirm the prompt text is recoverable.
findings.remedy: Accept as-is (files are gitignored) or drop inline -Prompt from stored args and re-resolve it from the log on demand; at minimum document that a never-started file contains the prompt.
